Now the Heki is awake he lets Kiln know "My intent is to spread word of this town, and its fight, in one of the largest conclaves of bards and historians in the multiverse.  If the hunger is not dead for good, as it is a threat to all reality, I plan on also talking to the masters of stories to find a solution for it.  By spreading the tales of this town, I ensure that their story never dies.  After that, My goal is simple, and is the same it has always been, go where ever I might be able to have the most impact in converting people with a destiny, into the people of that destiny.  Hence why I wanted your company, as I feel your path coincides with mine at least for a while.  You have a lot of good you can do out there.  As for Soloman, If he makes good on his deal with me, then I have faith he can change.  But he will need constant help for a while in being what he was meant to be, a champion for mortals.  He had to walk a very dark path to see who he truly is, and right now is standing at a fork in the road.  I desolate, empty, and meaningless existence, or a fulfilling one in which people believe in him, love him, and understand him to a degree.  What story teller would pass up on the opportunity to document that if he can find redemption?  So I have faith in him.  I have never been one to believe in gods, but if he can change into the person he needs to be, instead of the person he thinks he wants to be, that is a god I can believe in.  So it all depends on his actions tonight if he is welcome on our journey, and how the bards will speak of him for all time.  As long as the town can do their part to give him a chance, I feel there is a good chance he can someday find redemption."

Ozgur wakes up. There is a ringing in his ears. He realizes that it is the creature beneath the sheet, tweeting loudly. He smiles staring up at the ceiling. "Today is the day." Ozgur gets out of bed. He appraches the brass birdcage and gently lifts the sheet, just a bit, he whispers *"Don't come out today. Wait for me to return. If I don't, well..."* Ozgur sits quietly for a moment. "I will come back. I promise." He says with a smile. He grabs his things, and looks around the Warenui, one last time, at the Tekoteko meant to protect this place and his tribe, at the carved face of his grandfather. His face takes on a look of grim determination as he starts to head towards town.

Ozgur posts a message on his way into town. ```This place is my home, and I am willing to die for it. I witnessed the meeting between Solomon and Heki, and I believe there is a chance he will do the right thing.
